key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produces denser, harder Cr3C2–NiCr coatings with substantially better wear resistance than conventional APS, but it does not noticeably improve high-angle erosion performance.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical coating applications, axial-feed HV-APS offers a practical route to improve coating quality and tribological durability without changing the base cermet chemistry.
method: APS on S235 steel using a single-electrode A60 torch with radial powder injection
HV-APS using a three-electrode Axial III torch with axial powder feeding
Compared porosity, microhardness, phase composition, erosion at 90°, and ball-on-disc wear
evidence_signal: HV-APS reduced porosity from 11.99% to 6.16%, increased hardness from 897 to 1141 HV0.2, and lowered wear volume from 3.90 to 2.85 mm3, while erosion rates remained nearly unchanged (0.20 vs 0.19 mg/g).
watch_item: The improvement is clear in tribology, but the similar erosion response suggests that service conditions with high-impact particle attack may still require additional design optimization.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
